subject: Burst slice handoff and SLO clarification
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Luke Harper <luke@cartflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Burst slice handoff and SLO clarification

Luke — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary traffic: interactive checkout assistant, short prompts (10-60 tokens user input), typical responses 30-250 tokens.
- Peak pattern: 6x crest lasting ~90s every 12 hours (marketing windows).
- Steady baseline: ~18 qps, average response 120 tokens.
- Streaming: yes for multi-turn sessions; KV cache is important to keep latency under 150ms tail for first token.

Open clarifying asks for sizing
1) Confirm peak tokens/sec target: you mentioned ~14k tokens/sec crest, can you confirm whether that is aggregated across all regions or US-only?
2) Concurrency target: do you want concurrency headroom for 2x burst concurrency or ~1.5x?
3) SLOs: you stated p95 end-to-end latency target of 250ms for non-streaming, and p95 first-token streaming target of 180ms — please confirm.
4) Long-running sessions: what fraction of sessions hold an open streaming connection >30s? (helps with slot sizing)

Attached: cartflow_token_profile.csv (sample traffic by minute), mutual_action_plan_v2.pdf (draft MA for pilot).

Proposed next steps
- You confirm the three items above (peak tokens/sec scoping, concurrency headroom, streaming fraction) by EOD Wed.
- We deliver a pilot sizing note and recommended Dedicated config (GPU pool + burst slots) by Fri.
- If numbers line up, we kick off a 2-week pilot with a canary route and 1-week smoke test.

If helpful, I can run a quick spreadsheet mapping tokens/sec to slot counts with two quantization profiles and share.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa on the Dedicated sku recommendation after your confirmation.

– Diego
Diego Fernandez
SRE / Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
--
attachments: mutual_action_plan_v2.pdf, cartflow_token_profile.csv

From: Luke Harper <luke@cartflow.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: CartFlow Ops <ops@cartflow.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 15:10:43 -0700
Subject: Re: Burst slice handoff and SLO clarification

Diego — quick answers inline. Thanks for the tidy recap.

> Confirm peak tokens/sec target: you mentioned ~14k tokens/sec crest, can you confirm whether that is aggregated across all regions or US-only?
We meant US-only for this stage. Global ramp later.

> Concurrency target: do you want concurrency headroom for 2x burst concurrency or ~1.5x?
Aim for 1.8x headroom — we prefer some buffer but don’t want to double capacity right away.

> SLOs: p95 end-to-end latency target of 250ms for non-streaming, and p95 first-token streaming target of 180ms — please confirm.
Those look right. If you can hit p95 250ms non-streaming and 180ms first-token streaming we’ll be very happy.

> Long-running sessions: what fraction of sessions hold an open streaming connection >30s?
Rough estimate: 7% of sessions sustain >30s, mostly for back-and-forth troubleshooting flows.

Attaching the minute-level sample you requested on the call — includes user vs assistant token split.

Luke
Luke Harper
Head of Product, CartFlow
luke@cartflow.com

attachments: cartflow_minute_sample_1000rows.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 17:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Burst slice handoff and SLO clarification

Internal notes / sizing checkpoints before we send pilot note to Luke:

Assumptions to validate
- US-only peak crest: 14k tokens/sec
- Steady-state: 18 qps * 120 tokens avg = ~2160 tokens/sec
- Streaming fraction: 7% long sessions; assume streaming concurrency ~= 0.07 * active sessions
- Concurrency headroom: 1.8x

Preliminary mapping (quick back-of-envelope)
- If we provision with the H100-80GB profile and q4_0 quantization target, rough slot math: 1 slot ~= 800 tokens/sec sustained. For crest of 14k tokens/sec, need ~18 slots (plus 1.8x headroom => 32 slots).
- For burst handling we recommend a Dedicated pool with 28 baseline slots and 8 burst slots (auto-burst to cloud or pre-warmed). This keeps steady costs reasonable while meeting the crest with fallback.

Questions for Diego
- Can you run the token->slot mapping with a float quant profile too (q8_x) to show cost delta?
- Should we include a short streaming-only routing path (fewer tokens/sec capacity but optimized for first-token latency)? That would reduce tail latency at the expense of more slots.

I’ll draft the pilot configuration and cost delta once Diego confirms the two quant profiles.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Luke Harper <luke@cartflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Burst slice handoff and SLO clarification

Luke — thanks for the confirmations. Quick summary and final asks so we can ship the pilot sizing doc tomorrow: 

Agreed numbers
- Region: US-only for initial pilot.
- Crest: 14,000 tokens/sec (US).
- Steady: ~2,160 tokens/sec baseline.
- Concurrency headroom: 1.8x.
- Streaming fraction: 7% long sessions (>30s).
- SLOs: p95 non-streaming 250ms, p95 first-token streaming 180ms.

What we’ll deliver by EOD Thu
- Pilot sizing note with two quant profiles (q4_0 and q8_x) mapping to slot counts and estimated cost (pdf).
- Recommended Dedicated pool config: baseline + burst plan, failover routing policy, TTL for KV cache.
- Mutual Action Plan link and draft DocuSign (for sign-off if pilot proceeds).

One request: please confirm that the crest number (14k tokens/sec) includes assistant tokens. The attached CSV I have consolidates both user+assistant; if you have a split version please send it and we’ll re-run the slot math.

If all good I’ll book a 30-min kickoff for next Tue to walk through the pilot config and measurement plan.

Cheers — will follow up with the pilot note.

– Diego
Diego Fernandez
SRE / Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
